about.heading: About The Author
about.bioP2: Superheroes have been a part of my life since I watched and rewatched the first Captain America movie as a toddler in our family’s Honda Odyssey. Having grown up surrounded by their fantastical mythos, both in film and on paper, it was a no-brainer for me to start a blog talking about some of my favorite characters. I’ve been plummeting and diving and digging and falling down the quantum physics rabbit hole for nearly a year now, and connecting those interests with my childhood fixations is virtually a dream come true. I hope you guys enjoy every step of the way as much as I have, and happy reading!                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        Be sure to follow the instagram @quantumoffthepanels !!                                For any inquiries, hit up quantumoffthepanels@gmail.com.

amplitudeDial.title: The amplitude dial

predict.question: Turn the phase dial — only the phase, leaving the first dial alone. What happens to the two probability bars?
predict.because: Phase is invisible to a measurement on a single qubit. It's real, and it's doing something — but nothing you can see from here. Hold onto that; it's next week's whole story.

amplitudeDial.watchForLive: the bars never stop moving. The odds are exact; the outcome simply hasn't happened yet.
amplitudeDial.watchForCollapsed: the sphere has snapped to a pole. That IS the state now — the superposition is gone.

controls.lockedNote: The dials are dead. You don't have a superposition any more — you have an answer. Reset to prepare a new one.

captions.failing: the state is intact. i would know.
captions.lockedTemplate: it is |{outcome}⟩. from here, it was always going to be.
captions.phaseTurns: the phase turns. nothing turns with it.
captions.near0: it is |0⟩ and it will be |0⟩. there is nothing to wait for.
captions.near1: it is |1⟩ and it will be |1⟩. there is nothing to wait for.
captions.middle: it is neither. i see both. neither is happening.
captions.leaning0: it leans toward |0⟩. leaning is not being.
captions.leaning1: it leans toward |1⟩. leaning is not being.

speech.failing1: I observed it without disturbing it.
speech.failing2: The state is unchanged. I would know.
speech.lockedTemplate2: From here it was always going to be |{outcome}⟩. From a moment ago it was not going to be anything at all.
speech.locked3: I do not find this difficult.

violation.attempted: read the state without disturbing it
violation.why: The reading was real — and taking it is what destroyed the thing you were reading. There was never a hidden answer sitting underneath waiting to be checked. Reset and turn the dials again: nothing about that state was ever a 0 or a 1.

dial.pocketP1: This diagram is a Bloch Sphere: a visualization of a state that combines both phases along the equator (direction) and binary basis states at the poles (proximity to both 0 and 1).
dial.pocketP2: The vector you're controlling right now combines those pieces of information about our superposition!

watchersQuestion.title: The Watcher's question

predict.question: Take a qubit that is definitely UP. Ask 'up or down?' a hundred times and you get UP a hundred times. Now ask it 'left or right?' — what comes back?
predict.because: A state that is perfectly certain about one question can be perfectly undecided about another. The certainty was never a property the qubit had on its own — it was a property of the question you kept asking.

watchersQuestion.watchFor: the certainty table. Watch it move between rows — and never add up to more than it started with.

ending.line1: Seven questions, and the pattern is already the whole lesson: every answer that taught him something also cost him one he already had.
ending.kicker: There is no way to watch without choosing what to stop knowing. The vow was never available to him.

ledger.heading: What can be predicted right now
ledger.note: Notice what happened to the other rows when you asked.

pocket.label: What am I looking at?
pocket.p1: The circle is every state this qubit can be in. Up is ↑, down is ↓, and the arrow is the qubit itself. There's no phase in play this week, so the picture is flat and complete — nothing is hidden behind it.
pocket.p2: The dashed line is the question you asked. A measurement always has a direction: you don't ask "what is it?", you ask "is it this way or that way?" The answer can only ever be one of the two ends of that dashed line, so after asking, the arrow snaps onto it.
pocket.p3: Which is why certainty moves around instead of accumulating. Line the arrow up with one question and you've lined it up sideways to another, and sideways means a coin flip. Ask that second question and the arrow snaps again — abandoning everything the first answer told you.
pocket.p4: The uncomfortable part: before you asked, there was no answer waiting. A qubit pointing ↑ isn't secretly left or right. It genuinely has no left-or-right answer until a question forces one into existence.

violation.law: There is no view from nowhere.
violation.why: Nothing happened, and nothing was learned. A measurement is not a passive gaze that reveals what was already there — it is a specific question, and without one there is no answer to receive. Uatu's vow only holds while he learns nothing.

bothPaths.title: Both paths

predict.question: In week 1 the phase dial did nothing at all. Now the two routes are allowed to meet before anything is measured. What does that same dial do?
predict.choiceSweep: Sweeps him from one rod to the other
predict.choiceBoth: Sends him to both rods at once
predict.because: Phase was never invisible — it was only invisible to a measurement taken before the routes could meet. Let them meet, and phase decides everything about where he lands.

bothPaths.watchFor: the two dials. Turn them together and nothing happens — only the difference between them is real.

diagCaptions.bloch: the state — phase is longitude, odds are height
diagCaptions.fringe: the fringe — P(D0) against phase difference

voice.watchedLine: Someone was watching the lower lane, so there was only ever one of me. One of me has nothing to cancel against — the dials might as well be furniture.
voice.inPhaseLine: Both of me turned up at the same rod. In step, we just add. Nothing clever about it.
voice.outOfPhaseLine: Okay. Both of me sprinted at the other rod and neither of me got there. Half a turn out of step and we cancel — so I land at the one I wasn't aiming for. I didn't vanish. I showed up somewhere else.
voice.partialLine: Half in step, so it could've gone either way. Run it again and you might get the other rod.

pocket.label: What am I looking at?
pocket.p1: One Flash reaches the accelerator and doesn't pick a route — he takes both, which is why two blurs leave the splitter. He's moving far too fast to see properly; what you're watching is the light he leaves behind.
pocket.p2: Each dial delays one copy. That delay is phase. Turn both dials together and nothing happens at all — only the difference between them is real. A phase that everything shares is undetectable in principle, not merely hard to measure.
pocket.p3: Where the routes meet, the two halves of him add together. In step they reinforce and he lands at one rod every time. Half a turn out of step they cancel — and he lands at the other rod every time. He is never destroyed. Cancelling here means arriving there.
pocket.p4: Watch the sphere while you turn a dial: the arrow swings around without ever changing height, and height is what sets the odds. That is exactly why phase did nothing in week 1. Only when the routes recombine does the arrow tilt — longitude becomes latitude, and the phase you couldn't see turns into odds you can.

violation.law: You can know the route, or you can have the interference. Never both.
violation.attempted: watch which route he takes and still see the copies cancel
violation.why: Look at the ring: there's only one of him now. He isn't running both routes, so there aren't two things to add together — and with nothing to add, there is nothing to cancel. The fringe has gone flat and the dials do nothing. Stop watching and he splits again.
